# Salah-Eddine Elouali

> Official personal website of Salah-Eddine Elouali, a security researcher and final-year M2 systems, networks, and security engineering student focused on offensive security.

Salah-Eddine Elouali publishes online as `saladin0x1`. His work and interests center on offensive security, vulnerability research, network internals, and system behavior. This domain is his canonical personal website.

## Canonical Pages

- [Home](https://saladin.su/): Personal profile, current status, social links, and links to security writing and research.
- [Shadow Cat](https://saladin.su/cat/): Standalone interactive animation created for the site.
- [Sitemap](https://saladin.su/sitemap.xml): Machine-readable index of public pages.

## Writing

- [CleanseMeMaybe — Craft CMS RCE via condition.config](https://saladin.su/articles/cleanse-me-maybe/): How a JSON string walked past Craft CMS's config sanitizer. CVE-2026-78416, CVSS 8.8, fixed in Craft CMS 5.10.6 / 4.18.2.
- [Flat-Pack Security — redacted SQL injection to RCE case file](https://saladin.su/articles/flat-pack-security/): How an unauthenticated forgot-password SQL injection became OS command execution across three markets, followed by a 71-day bounty wait. Vendor identifiers and sensitive evidence are redacted.
- [Origin of Evil — postMessage origin-check bypass to DOM XSS](https://saladin.su/articles/origin-of-evil/): One missing negation in a ~indexOf origin check opened innerHTML and cookie-injection sinks on storefronts. Wildcard-DNS origins, SVG-namespace payloads, and an attack fully compliant with RFCs 1034, 1035, 6454, 8555, and the CA/Browser Forum requirements. Redacted case file.
- [Working on It — public API key and remediation theater](https://saladin.su/articles/working-on-it/): A public-by-design client key retained read, write, content-publishing, and notification capabilities. Five months later, symptom-level image filtering and object-scoped rate limits still missed the authorization failure. Names and operational details are redacted.
- [The Crowd Leech — grayware extension case file](https://saladin.su/articles/the-crowd-leech/): Static reverse engineering of a recommended Chrome extension: whole-DOM harvesting, bystander shipping, server-directed upload gating, internal API tapping, and credit-wallet resale. The public thread that prompted the analysis is preserved as redacted screenshots, ending on why deletion is not discourse. Byte-offset anchored evidence in the public repo.
- [No Light — a redacted RASP bypass case file](https://saladin.su/articles/no-light/): How two libc interposers forged a clean world for a mobile RASP: /proc and system properties read through hookable calls, the runtime's own key gates verifying the forgery, plaintext on disk with every check green past 110 seconds. The raw-syscall fix, merged upstream by the vendor's CEO, kills the same attack at second 29. Advisory declined as "brand new with no active usage." Vendors renamed, receipts on the public tape, PoC held per coordinated disclosure.

## Research

- [State of Sec Morocco 2026 — Project Site](https://stateofsec.ma): Canonical project site for the survey, linked from the home page research widget.
- [State of Sec Morocco 2026 — White Paper](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23947850): First edition of an open, anonymous community survey of Morocco's cybersecurity people. 380+ respondents, all 12 regions plus the diaspora, October 31 to November 15, 2026. 52 pages covering careers, pay, bug bounty, tools, AI, morale, and the Moroccan Cyber Sentiment Index (43.6/100). Open access, CC BY 4.0.
- [State of Sec Morocco 2026 — Aggregated Results](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24337485): Open dataset behind the White Paper: shares for 50 of 52 questions, published breakdowns, and the sentiment index in JSON, with the full questionnaire. Aggregates only, no individual answers. ODbL. Also mirrored at github.com/saladin0x1/stateofsec.ma.
